note: General industry links, each with its own source. They show what a mineral can become. They do not trace Chhattisgarh's ore to any plant, product or buyer. `inState` means a source on this page records that material being made in Chhattisgarh.

edges.text: Almost all iron ore goes to steelmaking: 98% of US shipments.
Most of a neodymium magnet's weight is iron.
LFP means lithium iron phosphate: the battery's cathode contains iron.
Integrated steel mills use metallurgical coke made from coal.
Coal tar can become needle coke, then battery anode material. Tata Steel reports a pilot plant.
Silicon metal is made by reducing quartz with carbon, and coal is one of the carbon sources.
In 2024 coal was the largest single source of electricity for data centres worldwide, about 30%. In India, the IEA projects renewables will overtake it by 2035.
Solder is one of tin's main uses: 11% of US use.
Machines that print the most advanced chips make their light by firing lasers at droplets of molten tin.
Flat glass is made by floating molten glass on a bath of molten tin.
Bauxite is refined into alumina, and most alumina is smelted into aluminium.
Gallium is mostly recovered as a by-product of processing bauxite.
Some bauxite goes into cement.
Steelmaking is the largest market for lime, which is made from limestone.
Limestone goes into cement, including portland-limestone cement.
Limestone is a standard ingredient of flat glass.
Dolomitic lime is used as a flux in steelmaking.
Dolomite is a standard ingredient of flat glass.
The Pidgeon process makes magnesium metal from calcined dolomite.
Transformers need grain-oriented electrical steel, and shortages have held up grid equipment.
These magnets go into motors for electric vehicles and machines.
LFP made up over 55% of EV batteries deployed worldwide in 2025, up from nearly 50% in 2024.
Artificial graphite is a common lithium-ion battery anode.
Silicon metal can be purified into semiconductor-grade polysilicon.
It can also be purified into solar-grade polysilicon.
In the IEA's base case, data centres use about 945 TWh by 2030, up from about 415 TWh in 2024.
Solder joins components on the circuit boards of electronic devices.
EUV light at 13.5 nm is how the smallest chip features are printed.
Gallium arsenide and gallium nitride make chips and light devices: 73% of US gallium goes to chips.
Transport is aluminium's largest use: 36% of US use.
Electrical uses take 9% of US aluminium.
Solar cover glass is low in iron, and ordinary limestone and dolomite can carry too much, so purity matters.
Most primary magnesium goes into castings, mainly for vehicles.
